accepted.why: The words are typed into a real input, which runs to the count, shows the text cursor and keeps its words inside its box; the pack draws them in a span as wide as the words
The count's automatic left margin resolves to nothing beside the input that fills the box; the count sits where the pack's does, which its box shows
At 200 % text the pack's span wraps the long name onto a second line and its box grows; a real input keeps one line and scrolls its words, as a phone's own fields do

On glass, the pack's reset for the cell's vote count (.sheet .count, a dark badge) also takes the halo from the field's light count, which its class shares; the kit keeps the halo on light words on glass, as the pack's glass rule intends

At 200 % text in a phone root (the shell's, which the glass cases sit in), a row with a value puts the value under its title, the pack's own large-text rule for rows (#228): in the pinned pack the title and the value run into each other there. The row is a grid, and its icon keeps its 12 px as a margin
What follows a row whose value went under its title moves down by that line
The list grows by the line its rows' values took under their titles

At 200 % text in a phone root (the shell's, which the glass cases sit in), a row puts its value under its title, the kit 0.5.0 rule (#228), now also when the value is a pill, as the Promise rows give it: in the pinned pack the pill keeps its place and squeezes the title onto narrow lines, where a longer title is cut
At 200 % text the pack's two long options squeeze their icons below the 18 px they are drawn at (to 12.8 and 11.4 px); the kit's icons keep their 18 px, as at 100 %

At 200 % in a phone root (the shell's, which the glass cases sit in), a stacking segmented control puts one option per row, the kit 0.5.0 rule (#228's .seg[data-stack]); the pinned pack keeps the two options side by side, squeezed
